**Allowed origins.** The `cors({ origin: (origin) => ... })` middleware in `worker/src/index.ts:19-35` decides this. It echoes the origin back only if it matches one of these:
- exactly `http://localhost:4200`
- any origin ending in `.pages.dev`
- any origin ending in `.workers.dev`

A request with no `Origin` header, or any other origin, gets `null`, so no CORS headers are sent. The other CORS settings in the same block:
- `allowMethods`: GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS
- `allowHeaders`: `Content-Type`, `Authorization`
- `maxAge`: 86400

**Adding a custom domain.** Edit the `if` condition at `worker/src/index.ts:23-27`, inside that `origin` function, and add one more clause:
```ts
origin === 'https://app.example.com' ||
```
- Use an exact match, including scheme, and no trailing slash. Use `endsWith` only if you want a whole suffix allowed.
- Don't put it in an array. Hono compares array entries as exact strings, so wildcards don't work there (`worker/src/index.md` and `DEPLOYMENT_NOTES §4`).
- `endsWith('.pages.dev')` is a loose suffix test. If you copy it for a custom domain, use `endsWith('.example.com')` with the leading dot, so `evilexample.com` can't match.

After the edit, update the CORS line in `worker/src/index.md` (Responsibilities) so the doc matches the code. I haven't checked whether `docs/DEPLOYMENT_NOTES.md` or `SETUP.md` also list the origins.

I didn't open `frontend/src/environments/environment.md`. If the custom domain is the frontend's, that doc describes the build-time API URL and Pages config, which this CORS check doesn't cover.
